confidence_notes: Restaurant, beer and coffee anchors come from aggregated crowd-sourced cost-of-living data found by web search. A summary citing Numbeo via Expatica, around June 2026, gave an inexpensive meal at about CHF 37 (range CHF 26-68), a three-course meal for two at about CHF 105 (range CHF 84-126) and a 0.5 L draught beer at about CHF 7.90. Other sources put a cappuccino at about CHF 5-5.20. These figures were adjusted slightly for summer tourist-area pricing in July 2026. The inexpensive meal was set below the crowd-sourced average because that average looked high. The searches found no aggregated cocktail or house-wine-by-the-glass prices, only single luxury-hotel bar menus such as sparkling wine at CHF 11-19 per 10 cl. Cocktail (about CHF 18) and wine (about CHF 9 per 1 dl) are therefore estimates based on how those drinks are usually priced relative to beer in Switzerland. They are less certain. The CHF-to-USD conversion uses a model assumption of about 1.22 USD per CHF for July 2026, which was not checked by search and adds roughly 5% uncertainty. All accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates for Lucerne's peak July season, not based on live listings. Lucerne has few hostels and high summer demand, so dorm and private-room prices could vary by about ±20%.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are based on Swiss urban averages, with Lucerne placed at or slightly above them because it is a major tourist hub. Comparable cities are Zurich and Bern for food and drink, and Interlaken for peak-season tourist accommodation demand.
